reports.verdict: EVgo cut its 2026 revenue and stall-build targets again, and the $2.00 takeover bid from majority owner LS Power now matters more than the quarter.

takeaways.label: Second guidance cut
takeaways.text: 2026 revenue outlook fell to $375-400M from $400-430M, new stalls to 1,075-1,275 from 1,350-1,625, and the EBITDA loss widened to $15-30M. Management blamed softer charging volumes and fewer, better sites.

takeaways.label: Core charging is growing
takeaways.text: Charging revenue rose 29% to $72M, but total revenue slipped 1% to $91.4M because partner-build (eXtend) revenue halved to $16M. Charging per stall fell 4% to 283 kWh a day.

takeaways.label: Buyout bid pending
takeaways.text: LS Power, with about 56% of the votes, offered $2.00 a share in cash on Nov. 2. A special committee is reviewing it, and management declined further comment.

takeaways.label: Losses and borrowing grow
takeaways.text: Net loss widened to $49.2M from $28.4M. Cash fell to $98.7M from $151M at year-end, and long-term debt rose to $312M from $204M. Management cited about $787M of liquidity.

reports.verdict: Berkshire is buying back its own stock at a much faster pace as GEICO's profit halves and core earnings slip.

takeaways.label: Buybacks accelerate
takeaways.text: Berkshire repurchased about $9.6 billion of its own shares in the quarter, double the prior quarter's $4.5 billion, and $14.4 billion for the year. Another $2 billion followed in October.

takeaways.label: GEICO profit halves
takeaways.text: GEICO's pre-tax profit nearly halved to $982 million as claims costs rose; the share of premiums paid out in claims climbed to 76.6% from 71.5%.

takeaways.label: Core earnings dip
takeaways.text: Operating earnings fell 5.8% to $12.7 billion. Rail, utilities and manufacturing grew, but weaker insurance profit and lower investment income outweighed them.

takeaways.label: Cash pile shrinks
takeaways.text: Berkshire still holds a very large cash pile. Buybacks and the $6.8 billion Taylor Morrison purchase, which closed in July, are now drawing it down.

reports.verdict: Moderna swung to a quarterly profit on a big international COVID sales beat, but the stronger cash outlook mostly comes from new debt.

takeaways.label: Big revenue beat
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 29% to $1.31B against about $885M expected, driven by international COVID deliveries. Full-year growth guidance rose to 15%–25% from up to 10%.

takeaways.label: Profit, with caveats
takeaways.text: Net income was $162M versus a $200M loss a year ago, helped by 27% lower R&D. Most of the quarter's sales were still uncollected at quarter-end.

takeaways.label: Cash boost is borrowed
takeaways.text: Year-end cash is now seen at $8.1–8.3B, up from $4.7–5.2B. About $2.6B of that is net proceeds from new convertible notes. The CEO said early-2027 contract talks will show if volumes hold.

takeaways.label: Pipeline progress
takeaways.text: The FDA approved Moderna's flu shot, though the U.S. launch is limited this season. Melanoma vaccine intismeran cut recurrence or death risk 42% in Phase 3, with filings being prepared.

reports.verdict: Opendoor is buying many more homes and growing revenue, but selling them at thinner margins in a weak market. Losses widen, and Q4 is guided worse.

takeaways.label: Margins keep shrinking
takeaways.text: Contribution margin fell to 3.3% from 5.8% last quarter. Management blamed spring-bought homes selling into a weaker market with deeper price cuts, and expects another decline in Q4.

takeaways.label: Bigger bet on inventory
takeaways.text: Homes bought rose to 4,865 from 1,169 a year ago. Inventory reached $2.57B, funded mostly with debt, and operating cash flow was -$1.8B over nine months.

takeaways.label: Losses widen, profit goal slips
takeaways.text: Net loss was $218M against $90M a year ago. Q4 adjusted EBITDA loss is guided at $70M-$85M, and management admits it is behind on reaching profitability by year-end.

takeaways.label: Revenue growth, softer than hoped
takeaways.text: Revenue was $1.02B, up 12% from a year ago. Q4 is guided to grow at least 40%, off a weak $736M base.

reports.verdict: DraftKings turned its profit forecast sharply lower, because a roughly $700 million bet on its Predictions product will leave 2026 profit near $200 million.

takeaways.label: Profit forecast slashed
takeaways.text: 2026 adjusted EBITDA, a measure of operating profit, is now $175-275 million, down from $700-900 million. Predictions spending of $650-700 million drives the cut.

takeaways.label: Weak 2027 outlook
takeaways.text: 2027 profit is guided to $800 million-$1 billion, including about $300 million of Predictions spending. Coverage says that trails the roughly $1.12 billion Wall Street expected.

takeaways.label: Core business softer
takeaways.text: Core 2026 profit guidance is now $875-925 million, below the roughly $1 billion guided in August, citing iGaming investment and customer-friendly sports results. Q3 revenue rose 16% to $1.33 billion, but the net loss was $469 million.

takeaways.label: Predictions payback claim
takeaways.text: Predictions revenue is guided to $650-750 million in 2027. Robins said that even if sports contracts ended in July 2028, 2027 customers would pay back within four years.

reports.verdict: Cloudflare's growth sped up to 39%, its fastest in nearly four years, and it raised its full-year revenue outlook by about $100 million.

takeaways.label: Growth accelerating, outlook raised
takeaways.text: Revenue hit $782.5M, up 39% (36% last quarter). Full-year guidance rose to $2.963B from $2.864–2.870B, and Q4 is guided to $845–846M.

takeaways.label: Broad customer demand
takeaways.text: Cloudflare added over 158,000 paying customers, nearly double the prior record. Existing customers also spent more: net retention reached 122%, and large deals included an $11M AI-company contract.

takeaways.label: Margins squeezed, profits improving
takeaways.text: Gross margin fell to 72.4% (non-GAAP) from 75.3% a year ago, but operating margin rose to 17.5%. Free cash flow slipped to 10% of revenue from 13%.

takeaways.label: Still losing money on GAAP
takeaways.text: The GAAP operating loss was $67.9M, mostly from stock pay. Management reportedly expects GAAP profitability in Q4, well ahead of its 2028 target.

reports.verdict: Record sales came from Alani Nu, but costs keep squeezing margins, the flagship CELSIUS brand is still shrinking, and fourth-quarter growth will slow.

takeaways.label: Margins keep sliding
takeaways.text: Gross margin fell to 46.8% from 51.3% a year ago and 48.1% last quarter. Aluminum and diesel costs rose further, and management expects only high-40s for the full year.

takeaways.label: Alani Nu carries growth
takeaways.text: Alani Nu sales rose 24% to $410M, with a record seasonal flavor. CELSIUS brand sales fell 6% to $357M, and management said it is 'not yet where we want it to be.'

takeaways.label: Growth slows next
takeaways.text: Fourth-quarter growth is guided below the first three quarters. About $20-25M of shipments were pulled into Q3, and last year's quarter had a one-time inventory benefit. No numeric targets were given.

takeaways.label: Reorganization and fixes
takeaways.text: Brand-led leadership is now in place, with new presidents for CELSIUS and Rockstar. Management says 2027 'will look very different' for CELSIUS, with new flavors and a second North Carolina production line.

reports.verdict: PENN's casinos beat expectations and its online business guided to a first profitable quarter, but a $20 million full-year Interactive loss still stands.

takeaways.label: Online losses nearly gone
takeaways.text: Interactive lost $18.3 million versus $76.6 million a year ago. Management guides to an $18.7 million profit in Q4, a $20 million full-year loss, and profit in 2027.

takeaways.label: Casinos beat, outlook raised
takeaways.text: Casino revenue hit $1.5 billion with profit margin up for a third straight quarter. Full-year casino profit guidance rose $10 million to $1.973 billion.

takeaways.label: Debt falling, buybacks eyed
takeaways.text: Net debt fell to $1.8 billion from $2.2 billion at year-end. Management says share buybacks are 'front of mind' for 2027, after paying down debt.

takeaways.label: Alberta launch gaining fast
takeaways.text: Online sports betting in Alberta is nearing its Ontario market share after three months. The launch cost $20 million, which explains why 2026 Interactive is no longer breakeven.
